source_types.label: NLI: place of writing
source_types.short_description: An NLI MARC 751 place explicitly assigned the role “place of writing”. This is the strongest structured geographic statement currently available.

source_types.label: NLI: related place
source_types.short_description: An NLI MARC 751 place assigned the broader role “related place”. The catalogue establishes a relationship but does not necessarily identify a writing or production location.

source_types.label: NLI: production-place display
source_types.short_description: A place transcribed in MARC 260 as production metadata. It is retained independently from authority-controlled 751 places and requires catalog-context review.

source_types.label: Place inferred from colophon
source_types.short_description: A candidate historical place extracted from an NLI colophon transcription or note. It is not accepted automatically and must retain the quoted evidence and extraction method.

source_types.label: Place inferred from provenance note
source_types.short_description: A candidate place in a provenance or ownership note. It may represent one stage in a manuscript’s movement rather than its production location.

source_types.label: Present repository
source_types.short_description: The manuscript’s current holding institution and locality. This is useful for access and comparison, but is not historical production evidence.

source_types.label: Project sheet: geographic candidate
source_types.short_description: A place proposed in the project’s manuscript spreadsheet or research notes. It is a project-level interpretation and remains distinct from NLI catalogue fields.

source_types.label: External catalogue: geographic assertion
source_types.short_description: A place asserted by another catalogue, including historical catalogues. The catalogue identity, date, methodology, and quoted statement must accompany every assertion.

source_types.label: Researcher geographic interpretation
source_types.short_description: A project or scholarly interpretation connecting the manuscript to a place or region. Competing interpretations may coexist and must identify their author and rationale.

source_types.label: NLI: catalogued date
source_types.short_description: The human-readable date statement in MARC 260$c. The original wording, uncertainty, approximation, and precision are preserved.

source_types.label: NLI: MARC fixed-field date
source_types.short_description: A machine-oriented date encoded in MARC 008. It is retained as an independent candidate and should not silently override the fuller 260$c statement.

source_types.label: Date inferred from colophon
source_types.short_description: A candidate date extracted from a colophon transcription or note. This can be close to primary evidence but remains mediated by transcription and interpretation.

source_types.label: Modern gazetteer geometry
source_types.short_description: A modern point or administrative geometry used to locate a place concept. It is a display aid, not an assertion that historical boundaries were identical.

source_types.label: Historical gazetteer geometry
source_types.short_description: A time-bounded geometry supplied by an identified historical gazetteer. Coverage and boundary assumptions must be retained.

source_types.label: Scholarly regional interpretation
source_types.short_description: A time-bounded point, polygon, or fuzzy region representing an identified scholarly interpretation. Multiple overlapping or conflicting geometries may coexist.
